title: Emotion Geometry in the KV Cache
subtitle: Corrected October 2026: story emotion is decodable from the KV cache, but not beyond a text (TF-IDF) baseline
abstract: When a language model reads a short third-person story, sent as a user message, whose character was written to feel one of 30 emotions, the requested emotion can be decoded from its KV cache far above chance, but a preregistered test finds that the cache probe the paper describes does not read it better than a text (TF-IDF) classifier on the story's words: 35.8% against 38.2% on the 30 emotions (chance 3.3%), with a 95% interval for the difference of -6.4 to +1.6 points that excludes the 3-point gain the test required (Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled, 900 stories). On a binary split of ten emotions (n = 300) that confounds valence with arousal, cache readouts separate the halves slightly better than text (TF-IDF), AUROC 0.985 against 0.967, a registered secondary result. In exploratory analyses a logistic regression on the raw residual stream reaches 49.4%, above both the cache probe and a tuned text (TF-IDF) baseline (44.8%). Projected through W_K, residual-stream emotion directions line up with the emotions' assigned valence (|rho| = 0.862 at layer 35), but the projection does not predict the cache's measured geometry (Mantel rho = 0.090), so it remains a candidate route. The labels are the emotions a generator was asked to write, about characters rather than users. This version corrects a May 2026 paper that read them as the user's emotional state and withdraws its injection test and its direction-versus-shape claim.
